claims.text: The starting material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser sintering can introduce pores into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing pores will reduce the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The porous material will retain a continuous, load-bearing network of high-entropy-alloy phases.
Retention of a continuous load-bearing alloy network will maintain mechanical strength despite the pores.
Porous, selectively laser-sintered HfMoTaTiZr can have reduced density without sacrificing its room-temperature mechanical properties.
Porous, selectively laser-sintered HfMoTaTiZr can have reduced density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The proposed performance boundary includes both tensile and compressive loading from room temperature to 1000 °C.
Samples with varying pore fractions will be compared by measuring density, tensile strength, and compressive strength at room temperature and 1000 °C.
A tensile- or compressive-strength reduction greater than 10% at either room temperature or 1000 °C relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will reject the hypothesis.
The effect of pores on elevated-temperature mechanical properties is uncertain and requires experimental verification.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, whereas the predicted outcome allows a minimal sacrifice and the rejection rule permits strength losses of up to 10% without falsification.
